central_claim: Historical shipment/container identifiers survive across support types, languages and documentary states. They are relational keys, not markers of a single material or linguistic class.

cross_class_findings: Shipment/container identifiers occur on Nepali hand-made paper, imported paper and machine-made paper.
They occur on local-language source texts, English derivative/copy states and bilingual/multilingual metadata surfaces.
The same identifier system can therefore link documents across material and linguistic classes.
Historical container identity must be coded separately from support, language and modern shelfmark.
source_control_rules: Do not reconstruct unread identifier values omitted by the online catalogue.
Do not equate box/sack numbers across dates without content-level confirmation.
A cover number proves historical container assignment, not direct textual descent.
Identifier language does not determine the language or origin of the underlying document.
